pins.title: Child carrier digging into your shoulders?
pins.sub: Let your hips carry the weight.
pins.pinTitle: How to make a hiking child carrier more comfortable: fit steps for parents, hips first
pins.description: On a well-fitted child carrier, your hips carry most of the weight, not your shoulders. Set the torso length to your back, buckle the hip belt on your hip bones, then snug the shoulder straps, load lifters and sternum strap, and set your child's seat height. Our Trail Journal walks through each fit step for family hikes.

pins.title: Icy trail this weekend?
pins.sub: Grip for your boots, warm socks inside.

Our Icy Trail Kit pairs stainless steel chain ice cleats that stretch over the boots you already wear with cushioned merino wool crew socks to keep feet warm. For winter hikes, icy sidewalks and dog walks. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

Sizes S to XL. A practical gift for anyone who hikes or walks with a dog. Gear ships in 6-13 business days.

pins.title: Holiday travel day? Pack warm socks.
pins.sub: Cold gates, long flights, cozy feet.
pins.pinTitle: Warm merino wool socks for holiday travel: cozy cushioned crew socks for flights and airports
pins.description: Cold airport gates, drafty planes, long car rides to family: cushioned crew socks with 80% merino wool keep feet warm without getting sweaty, and they stay fresh through a long travel day. For travel, home, work and the trail.

pins.title: Slow cabin mornings, warm feet
pins.pinTitle: Cozy merino wool socks for cabin mornings: warm cushioned crew socks for cold days
pins.description: Coffee on the porch, frost on the steps, boots waiting by the door. Cushioned 80% merino wool crew socks feel soft, not itchy, and keep feet warm on cold mornings at the cabin, at home or on the trail. Two sizes and four colors.

pins.title: Cold toes on a winter hike?
pins.sub: Loose laces and dry socks help.
pins.pinTitle: How to keep your feet warm on a winter hike: lacing, dry socks and boots with room for your toes
pins.description: Laces pulled too tight cut blood flow to your toes, and damp socks pull heat away fast. Leave a little room in your boots, carry a dry pair of wool socks to change into, and keep moving at breaks. Our Trail Journal has the full list for cold-weather hikes.

pins.title: Winter is Joshua Tree season
pins.sub: Cool days, cold nights. Plan for both.
pins.board: Best Day Hikes in US National Parks
pins.pinTitle: Joshua Tree National Park in winter: trip planning guide with day hikes, camping and desert safety
pins.description: Cooler months are a popular time to hike Joshua Tree, but desert nights can drop below freezing, so pack warm layers along with plenty of water. Our Joshua Tree Trip Planning Guide covers campground reservations, a 1-day plan, hike cards like Hidden Valley and Barker Dam, and a desert water plan. Instant PDF download.
